title: How Many Web APIs Evolve Following Semantic Versioning?
authors: Souhaila Serbout, Cesare Pautasso
central_claim: Across 3,075 OpenAPI histories (506,273 changes of 195 types), 1,970 APIs do not always signal breaking changes with a major version; only 517 consistently do (best case).
cite_claim: Spec-level breaking changes are common in public Web APIs and version numbers do not reliably announce them; even the spec-diff method leaves about one third of changes undecidable, and the authors concede subtle changes may be missed.
location: Abstract; Sec. 3 (change classification: 96 breaking, 66 non-breaking, 33 undecidable types); Sec. 7.1 Threats to validity
quote: Not all changes may be documented or detected, especially if they are subtle or indirect, possibly underestimating the true impact of API changes
relevance: Deep-read. Largest web-API spec-evolution study; uses oasdiff, so it is also the upper bound of what spec-diff sees. Its own threat-to-validity names the gap fiks targets.

title: Breaking Changes in Software Ecosystems: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Juntao Chen, Tingting Bi, Yanlin Wang, Patanamon Thongtanunam
central_claim: 97 primary studies: 43 detection approaches reach high accuracy on syntactic breaks but limited coverage on behavioral ones; behavioral breaks evade static detection and need test-based oracles.
cite_claim: Behavioral breaking changes preserve the interface but alter runtime semantics, and current detection tools cover them poorly; the review names LLM-augmented behavioral contract inference and automated repair as open opportunities.
location: Abstract; Sec. 3.1 and 3.1.2 (Behavioral Breaking Changes); Sec. 7.2.1
quote: Behavioral breaking changes preserve the syntactic interface but alter runtime semantics.
relevance: Deep-read. 2026 synthesis that frames the exact gap (behavioral breaks, detection + repair) and states 'The bottleneck is contract generation, not verification' (Sec. 7).

title: Towards Better Comprehension of Breaking Changes in the NPM Ecosystem
authors: Dezhen Kong, Jiakun Liu, Lingfeng Bao, David Lo
central_claim: Of 1,519 documented breaking changes in 381 npm projects, 'change behavior' breaking changes are the largest category (68.1%); 19% of documented breaking changes cannot be detected by regression testing.
cite_claim: In a large library ecosystem, about two thirds of documented breaking changes are behavioral rather than signature changes.
quote: Change Behavior BCs make up the largest proportion of all BC types (68.1%).
relevance: Deep-read. Best available estimate of the behavioral share of breaking changes; library (npm) not web API, so use as proxy evidence only.

title: Differential Regression Testing for REST APIs
authors: Patrice Godefroid, Daniel Lehmann, Marina Polishchuk
central_claim: Comparing responses of different service/spec versions on the same RESTler-generated request sequences found 14 regressions across 17 Azure networking API versions: 5 in specifications and 9 in the services themselves.
cite_claim: Service regressions (previously working requests broken while client/spec version is held fixed) are distinct from spec regressions and were the majority of regressions found in Azure networking APIs.
location: Abstract; Sec. 2.3 Regressions in REST APIs; Sec. 4.6 Threats to Validity
quote: detected 14 regressions in total, 5 of those in the official API specifications and 9 regressions in the services themselves.
relevance: Deep-read. Closest prior art for detecting behavioral drift without a spec change; strongest baseline idea (version-differential testing). Requires both versions reachable; outputs diffs, not fixes.

title: I Depended on You and You Broke Me: An Empirical Study of Manifesting Breaking Changes in Client Packages
authors: Daniel Venturini, Filipe Roseiro Cogo, Ivanilton Polato, Marco A. Gerosa, Igor Scaliante Wiese
central_claim: About 12% of npm client packages were impacted by a manifesting breaking change in non-major updates; 44% were introduced in minor and patch releases; 21.9% were undocumented.
cite_claim: More than one-fifth of manifesting breaking changes were undocumented (existing claim C15).
quote: more than one-fifth of the manifesting breaking changes are undocumented
relevance: Reuses RESEARCH.md C15. Supports 'changelogs do not announce it'.

title: Experience Paper: A Study on Behavioral Backward Incompatibilities of Java Software Libraries
authors: Shaikh Mostafa, Rodney Rodriguez, Xiaoyin Wang
central_claim: Cross-version regression testing of 68 version pairs of 15 Java libraries found 296 behavioral backward incompatibilities in 52 pairs; most were not documented in API docs or release notes.
cite_claim: Behavioral backward incompatibilities are frequent and mostly undocumented; library-side regression tests detect a different distribution than the ones that break clients.
quote: the majority of behavioral backward incompatibilities are not well documented in API documents or release notes
relevance: Foundational evidence that behavioral (not signature) incompatibility is common and invisible in docs.

title: Understanding the Impact of APIs Behavioral Breaking Changes on Client Applications
authors: Dhanushka Jayasuriya, Valerio Terragni, Jens Dietrich, Kelly Blincoe
central_claim: Updating 30,548 Maven dependencies, 2.30% of updates had behavioral breaking changes that impacted client tests; most came in non-major updates.
cite_claim: Behavioral breaking changes reach client tests in a measurable fraction of dependency updates and mostly arrive in non-major versions.
quote: We found that 2.30% of these updates had behavioral breaking changes that impacted client tests.
relevance: Counter-weight: per-update rate of client-visible behavioral breaks is low (2.3%), which matters for the base rate a monitor sees. A LinkedIn excerpt reports a different figure (11.58%); use the conference abstract.

title: Historical and Impact Analysis of API Breaking Changes: A Large-Scale Study
authors: Laerte Xavier, Aline Brito, Andre Hora, Marco Tulio Valente
central_claim: 317 Java libraries, ~500K API changes: 27.99% break backward compatibility; frequency rises over time.
cite_claim: Existing claim C14 (library APIs, not web APIs).
location: Abstract (per RESEARCH.md C14) [verify: not re-opened in this pass]
quote: [verify] 27.99% of API changes break backward compatibility (RESEARCH.md C14 summary, not re-quoted here)
relevance: Reuse C14; signature-level only, so it under-counts behavioral breaks.

title: Breaking Bad? Semantic Versioning and Impact of Breaking Changes in Maven Central
authors: Lina Ochoa, Thomas Degueule, Jean-Remy Falleri, Jurgen Vinju
central_claim: Replication over 119,879 upgrades and 293,817 clients: 83.4% of upgrades comply with semantic versioning, contradicting the earlier Raemaekers et al. finding that ~1/3 of releases break.
cite_claim: Measured semver compliance of Java libraries is higher (83.4%) than earlier studies reported; results depend strongly on method and corpus.
location: Abstract; also restated in Serbout & Pautasso 2024, Sec. 2
quote: 119 879 Java library upgrades and 293 817 clients revealing that 83.4% of upgrades adhere to semantic versioning.
relevance: Contradiction source: static (signature) analyses disagree on how often breaks happen; static tools see only syntactic breaks. Quote is Serbout & Pautasso's restatement.

title: How Does Web Service API Evolution Affect Clients?
authors: Jun Li, Yingfei Xiong, Xuanzhe Liu, Lu Zhang
central_claim: Analysis of 5 popular web APIs (256 changed elements): 16 change patterns and 6 client-migration challenges specific to web APIs.
cite_claim: Web API clients face migration challenges that local-library clients do not, partly because they cannot stay on an old version.
location: Abstract [verify: abstract seen via search/DBLP only]
quote: [verify] analyzed the evolution of five popular web APIs, in total 256 changed API elements
relevance: Foundational web-API evolution study; no spec-vs-behavior split.

title: A Case Study of Web API Evolution
authors: S. M. Sohan, Craig Anslow, Frank Maurer
central_claim: Case study of web API version changes and how they are documented and communicated; documentation and change notices are often inadequate.
cite_claim: Inadequate documentation and change communication make web API changes break dependent applications.
location: Abstract [verify: abstract seen via AMiner/IEEE CS listing only]
quote: [verify] changes to a web API can break dependent applications (paraphrase of abstract)
relevance: Foundational; supports the communication-gap premise (with C16).

title: Web API Growing Pains: Loosely Coupled yet Strongly Tied
authors: Tiago Espinha, Andy Zaidman, Hans-Gerhard Gross
central_claim: Web API evolution imposes maintenance burden on client developers despite nominal loose coupling.
cite_claim: Existence only; findings not verified in this pass.
location: DBLP record [verify: full text not opened]
quote: [verify] title and venue confirmed via DBLP; no text quoted
relevance: Foundational web API client-impact study; cite only after a verifier opens it.

title: Microservice API Evolution in Practice: A Study on Strategies and Challenges
authors: Alexander Lercher, Johann Glock, Christian Macho, Martin Pinzger
venue_or_publisher: Journal of Systems and Software (ICSA 2025 journal-first); arXiv:2311.08175
central_claim: 17 interviews at 11 companies: change-impact analysis is effortful, change communication is ineffective, consumers stay on outdated versions.
cite_claim: Practitioners report ineffective communication of API changes and costly impact analysis, and call for automation.
quote: ineffective communication of changes
relevance: Industry-practice evidence for the premise; complements C16 survey.

title: Putting the Semantics into Semantic Versioning
authors: Patrick Lam, Jens Dietrich, David J. Pearce
central_claim: Version numbers cannot fully characterize compatibility; behavioral contracts are a promising input to semantic-versioning calculators.
cite_claim: Contracts (traditional and lightweight) are proposed as the input for judging whether an upgrade is safe.
quote: contracts (both traditional and lightweight) are a promising input to semantic versioning calculators
relevance: Conceptual precedent for outcome contracts as the compatibility oracle.

title: Deriving Semantics-Aware Fuzzers from Web API Schemas
authors: Zac Hatfield-Dodds, Dmitry Dygalo
central_claim: Schemathesis derives property-based fuzzers from OpenAPI/GraphQL schemas; in a comparison of 8 fuzzers on 16 services it found 1.4x-4.5x more unique defects than the runner-up.
cite_claim: Schema-derived property-based testing is the strongest open-source tool for finding schema violations and crashes in web APIs.
quote: derives structure- and semantics-aware fuzzers from web API schemas
relevance: Primary runnable baseline (MIT). Its oracle is the spec; it can catch type drift and lost writes but not unit or pagination drift under an unchanged permissive spec.

title: Schemathesis documentation: Checks reference; Stateful testing guide
authors: Schemathesis maintainers
central_claim: Built-in checks include response_schema_conformance and the stateful ensure_resource_availability and use_after_free; stateful links are inferred from the schema and Location headers.
cite_claim: Schemathesis checks response bodies against the schema and verifies that created resources are immediately accessible.
location: Checks reference: 'Core response validation' and 'Stateful behavior'; Stateful testing guide
quote: ensure_resource_availability: Verifies created resources are immediately accessible.
relevance: Important for fairness: this check may detect D3 (lost write) and response_schema_conformance may detect D5 (epoch number vs string date-time) with the unchanged vendor spec.

title: RESTler: Stateful REST API Fuzzing
authors: Vaggelis Atlidakis, Patrice Godefroid, Marina Polishchuk
central_claim: First stateful REST API fuzzer; infers producer-consumer dependencies from the spec; found 28 bugs in GitLab.
cite_claim: Stateful spec-driven fuzzing finds server errors in real cloud services.
quote: the first stateful REST API fuzzer
relevance: Runnable baseline (MIT, github.com/microsoft/restler-fuzzer); default oracle is 5xx plus checkers, so silent 200-OK drift is out of scope.

title: EvoMaster: AI-driven system test generation for Web APIs
authors: Andrea Arcuri et al. (WebFuzzing)
central_claim: White-box and black-box test generation for REST, GraphQL and RPC; more than 30 oracles incl. HTTP 500, schema mismatches, access-policy violations.
cite_claim: EvoMaster uses 30+ automated oracles, including schema mismatch, for black-box Web API testing.
quote: More than 30 oracles are currently used
relevance: Runnable black-box baseline (LGPL-3.0). Black-box mode works against any language.

title: Testing RESTful APIs: A Survey
authors: Amid Golmohammadi, Man Zhang, Andrea Arcuri
central_claim: Survey of 92 articles on REST API testing; many open challenges remain, including test oracles.
cite_claim: REST API testing research is large and growing, but oracle problems remain open.
quote: [verify] reviews 92 scientific articles on testing RESTful APIs
relevance: Survey anchor for related work.

title: AGORA: Automated Generation of Test Oracles for REST APIs
authors: Juan C. Alonso, Sergio Segura, Antonio Ruiz-Cortes
central_claim: Infers output invariants from observed requests/responses with an extended Daikon; 81.2% precision on 11 operations of 7 industrial APIs; detected 6 of 10 seeded output errors; revealed 11 bugs.
cite_claim: Invariants mined from API traffic serve as black-box test oracles with ~81% precision and catch ~60% of seeded output errors.
quote: AGORA achieved a total precision of 81.2% when tested on a dataset of 11 operations from 7 industrial APIs.
relevance: Closest prior art for inferring semantic invariants from v1 traffic (fiks contract inference). Runnable baseline for contract inference.

title: Test Oracle Generation for REST APIs (AGORA+)
authors: Juan C. Alonso, Michael D. Ernst, Sergio Segura, Antonio Ruiz-Cortes
central_claim: AGORA+ detects 106 invariant types; 80% precision on 25 operations from 20 industrial APIs; 48% of seeded errors; 32 bugs; PostmanAssertify emits JS assertions.
cite_claim: Traffic-mined invariants reach 80% precision on 25 operations of 20 APIs and detect 48% of seeded output errors.
quote: AGORA+ achieved a precision of 80% on 25 operations from 20 industrial APIs.
relevance: Replication package on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.14728849) and Docker image: runnable invariant-inference baseline over v1 traces.

title: A Multi-Agent Approach for REST API Testing with Semantic Graphs and LLM-Driven Inputs (AutoRestTest)
authors: Myeongsoo Kim, Tyler Stennett, Saurabh Sinha, Alessandro Orso
central_claim: MARL + semantic property dependency graph + LLM beats four black-box REST testing tools on coverage and fault detection across 12 services.
cite_claim: LLM-assisted REST testing improves coverage and server-error detection over prior black-box tools.
quote: AutoRestTest is the only tool able to trigger an internal server error in the Spotify service.
relevance: Latest LLM-era REST testing; still error-oriented oracle, so complementary not competing.

title: LogiAgent: Automated Logical Testing for REST Systems with LLM-Based Multi-Agents
authors: Ke Zhang, Chenxi Zhang, Chong Wang, Chi Zhang, YaChen Wu, Zhenchang Xing, Yang Liu, Qingshan Li, Xin Peng
central_claim: LLM multi-agent logical oracles over business logic found 234 logical issues in 12 REST systems with 66.19% accuracy.
cite_claim: LLM-judged business-logic oracles find logical issues beyond status codes but about a third of flags are not correct.
quote: 234 logical issues with an accuracy of 66.19%
relevance: Evidence for an LLM-judge monitor baseline and its precision ceiling.

title: MASTOR: A Multi-Agent Approach to Semantic Test Oracle Generation for RESTful APIs
authors: Sida Deng, Rubing Huang, Zhenzhen Yang, Man Zhang, Xuan Xie, Rongcun Wang
central_claim: Multi-agent LLM generation of semantic oracles from source; 75.4% mean mutation score on 13 projects; beats direct prompting (69.9% vs 39.8%) and SATORI.
cite_claim: LLM-generated semantic oracles for REST APIs substantially beat direct prompting on mutation score.
quote: MASTOR achieved an average mutation score of 75.4%, generating 10,022 oracles.
relevance: Latest (2026) semantic-oracle generation; offline, white-box, needs server source; no runtime capture or repair.

title: Multi-Agent LLM-based Metamorphic Testing for REST APIs
authors: Shehroz Khan, Abdullah Mughees, Gaadha Sudheerbabu, Tanwir Ahmad, Dragos Truscan
central_claim: ARMeta uses LLM agents to derive metamorphic relations for OpenAPI-documented REST APIs to address the oracle problem.
cite_claim: Metamorphic relations are an active 2026 answer to the REST oracle problem.
quote: the difficulty of assessing whether the output of an API call is correct
relevance: Related oracle work; no numbers in abstract.

title: oasdiff: OpenAPI Diff and Breaking Changes (BREAKING-CHANGES.md)
authors: oasdiff maintainers (Reuven Harrison et al.)
central_claim: oasdiff breaking compares two OpenAPI definitions and reports ERR (definite) and WARN (potential) breaking changes from hundreds of checks; it judges against the declared contract.
cite_claim: Spec-diff tools judge a change against the contract the OpenAPI document declares; identical documents yield no findings (existing claim C27).
quote: judges a change against the API contract your OpenAPI definition declares
relevance: Runnable baseline; by construction reports nothing on a byte-identical spec. Used by Serbout & Pautasso.

title: openapi-diff: Utility for comparing two OpenAPI specifications
authors: OpenAPITools
central_claim: Classifies spec changes as incompatible/compatible; CI flag --fail-on-incompatible.
cite_claim: openapi-diff classifies differences between two OpenAPI documents as compatible or incompatible.
quote: Only if API changes broke backward compatibility
relevance: Second spec-diff baseline (Java, Docker image).

title: Optic (opticdev/optic)
authors: Optic Labs (now part of Atlassian)
central_claim: Spec diff with breaking-change checks plus capture of test traffic to verify the spec; repository archived Jan 2026; Optic Labs joined Atlassian.
cite_claim: Optic compared OpenAPI versions and test traffic against the spec; the OSS repo is archived.
quote: Optic is MIT Licensed.
relevance: Runnable but unmaintained baseline; its capture mode updates the spec to match reality (opposite direction from fiks).

title: Prism validation proxy guide
authors: Stoplight
central_claim: prism proxy sits between client and upstream and reports discrepancies between traffic and the OpenAPI document; --errors turns mismatches into errors.
cite_claim: An OpenAPI validation proxy can flag live responses that do not match the declared schema.
quote: identify discrepancies between the OpenAPI document and any other server you designate as the target
relevance: Closest runnable analog of fiks's observe step at the vendor boundary (schema-only). Ideal 'schema-only proxy' baseline.

title: Specmatic
authors: Specmatic (znsio)
central_claim: Turns API specifications into executable contract tests and stubs; offers a spec-based backward-compatibility check.
cite_claim: Specmatic runs OpenAPI specs as executable contract tests against a service.
quote: Specmatic turns API specifications into executable contracts.
relevance: Optional baseline; oracle is still the spec.

title: How Pact works
authors: Pact Foundation
central_claim: Consumer tests produce a pact file of example interactions; the provider replays them and checks the response contains at least the expected data.
cite_claim: Consumer-driven contracts verify example interactions against the provider, which requires the provider to run the consumer's pacts.
location: How Pact works page, provider verification section
quote: each request is sent to the provider, and the actual response it generates is compared
relevance: Strongest pre-deployment alternative when the provider cooperates; third-party vendors (Stripe, GitHub) do not run their consumers' pacts.

title: PactFlow Bi-Directional Contract Testing: OpenAPI Specification Contracts
authors: SmartBear / PactFlow
central_claim: BDCT statically compares a consumer pact with the provider's OpenAPI document; the consumer contract is not replayed against provider code.
cite_claim: Bi-directional contract testing reduces to a static schema comparison.
location: BDCT guide [verify: seen via search summary; main guide URL returned 404 on fetch]
quote: [verify] statically compares the contracts down to the field level
relevance: Shows commercial contract testing converging on spec comparison, which cannot see spec-unchanged drift.

title: How API versioning works (Stripe docs)
authors: Stripe
central_claim: Stripe ships monthly non-breaking versions and twice-yearly majors; it deems new response properties and changes to the length or format of opaque strings backward-compatible.
cite_claim: Major providers define some response changes (new properties, opaque-string format changes, new event types) as non-breaking and expect clients to tolerate them.
quote: Changing the length or format of opaque strings, such as object IDs, error messages, and other human-readable strings.
relevance: Real-world basis for fiks's version-pinned vendor design and for false-positive risk: invariants must tolerate declared-compatible changes.

title: Upcoming changes to GitHub Events API payloads
authors: GitHub
central_claim: GitHub removed commit summaries/counts from push events and author_association from seven event types; brownout 2025-09-08, effective 2025-10-07.
cite_claim: A major API removed payload fields in place with the endpoint still returning 200, announced only in a changelog post.
quote: On October 7, 2025, we'll officially implement the above changes.
relevance: Real-world candidate for a field-removal drift (D2-like) with 200 OK; announced, so tests the 'changelogs go unread' premise rather than 'unannounced'.

title: GitHub changed their API without warning and broke our production system
authors: Stategraph / Terrateam
central_claim: The workflow-dispatch endpoint switched from 204 No Content to 200 with a JSON body while GitHub's OpenAPI schema still listed 204; clients validating 204 broke.
cite_claim: A live behavior change contradicted the provider's published OpenAPI schema and broke a production client.
quote: No deprecation notice. No changelog entry.
relevance: Real-bug candidate where the spec lagged the service. Single-party account; GitHub changelog 2026-02-19 later made run details opt-in via return_run_details [verify].

title: Workflow dispatch API now returns run IDs
authors: GitHub
central_claim: New optional return_run_details parameter returns 200 with run metadata; omitting it keeps 204.
cite_claim: GitHub later shipped the run-ID response as opt-in.
location: Changelog post [verify: seen via search summary only]
quote: [verify] Previously, this endpoint returned only a 204 No Content status code.
relevance: Pairs with stategraph post: behavior shipped ahead of spec, then formalized.

title: OpenAPI contract drift detection (Beeceptor docs)
authors: Beeceptor
central_claim: Detects drift between live traffic and the OpenAPI spec (schema, enum, status, auth, 'behavioral drift'); proposes AI-assisted spec patches merged after human approval.
cite_claim: Commercial drift monitors compare traffic to the spec and repair the spec, not the consuming code.
location: Drift types list; patch workflow section
quote: same contract, but different behavior
relevance: Market competitor in drift monitoring; fix direction is opposite to fiks (doc follows reality vs consumer code adapts).

title: Systems and Methods for Detecting Silent Backward-Incompatible API Contract Drift Using Runtime Structural-Semantic Fingerprints
authors: Harsh Agrawal, Isha Navanath Shinde (VISA)
central_claim: Learns endpoint-specific behavioral invariants from historical traffic and alerts on silent backward-incompatible drift.
cite_claim: Prior art exists for learning per-endpoint behavioral invariants from traffic to detect silent API drift; the disclosure stops at alerts.
location: Abstract (full PDF not read) [verify full text for test generation/repair]
quote: learning endpoint-specific behavioral invariants from historical API traffic
relevance: Novelty threat for the detection half of fiks; must be cited. Does not describe repro tests or repair (abstract only).

title: Postman Acquires Akita Software to Help Build the Future of API Observability
authors: Postman (press release)
central_claim: Akita discovers and monitors APIs by watching traffic without SDKs; acquired by Postman.
cite_claim: Traffic-based API discovery and monitoring is an established commercial category.
location: Press release [verify: content seen via search summary]
quote: [verify] automatically discovers and monitors APIs by watching API traffic
relevance: Industry consolidation signal (Akita to Postman, Optic to Atlassian).

title: From REST to MCP: An Empirical Study of API Wrapping and Automated Server Generation for LLM Agents
authors: Meriem Mastouri, Emna Ksontini, Amine Barrak, Wael Kessentini
central_claim: Of 116 official MCP servers, 88.6% are fully or partially REST-backed and ~92% implement tools as bare API wrappers.

quote: 88.6% of servers are fully or partially REST-backed
relevance: Key bridge: justifies the shop-mcp-wraps-vendor-api setup as representative.

title: BreakGuard: Towards Detecting Dependency Breaking Changes with LLM-Generated Tests
authors: Rachna Raj, Benoit Baudry, Diego Elias Costa
central_claim: LLM-generated per-call-site tests detect 30.3% (27/89) of real BUMP breaking changes at ~$0.90 per detection; less reliable for behavioral than crash-type changes.
cite_claim: Pre-emptive LLM test generation detects under a third of real breaking changes and is weakest on behavioral ones.
quote: we find LLM-generated tests to be more reliable for detecting crash-type breaking changes as opposed to behavioural BCs
relevance: 2026 competitor for the 'reproduce' step; supports using observed failures instead of guessed tests (C17-C19).

title: AutoGuard: Reporting Breaking Changes of REST APIs from Java Spring Boot Source Code
authors: Alexander Lercher, Christian Bauer, Christian Macho, Martin Pinzger
central_claim: Derives OpenAPI from Spring Boot source for two versions, diffs them and reports breaking changes in PR/MR CI.
cite_claim: Provider-side tools can derive specs from source and diff them in CI, but remain spec-level.
location: Tool demo abstract [verify: details from search summary]
quote: [verify] Reporting breaking changes of REST APIs from Java Spring Boot source code (title)
relevance: Provider-side, needs provider source; not applicable to third-party vendors.
